gen-dafont-electroharmonix-fs-be-vietnam: Striking up top, Electroharmonix splits words into separate, open-handed letters. Be Vietnam Pro follows in sans strokes like a bent steel rod, with curve endings that keep their distance, so the display face gets room to shout.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-fs-bespoke-sa: Bespoke Sans is a sharp sans-serif with generous space between curve ends and stems, and a more moderate lowercase height than Electroharmonix. Bump its size up a notch.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-fs-hoover: Electroharmonix breaks each word into spaced, open-handed letters, while Hoover answers in a classic serif with a generous entry into the e's eye. Refined next to robust, that is the whole appeal.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-fs-nunito: Nunito reads friendly and current, with big round lowercase bowls. Electroharmonix is best at striking, gapped display letters, while Nunito, a plain sans, is best at sitting quietly and letting the words flow.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-fs-pilcrow-ro: Electroharmonix hits hard with its gapped, open-handed curves and a sizable x-height. And Pilcrow Rounded, an unmodulated sans-serif with curves that refuse to close, backs it up warmly, so the heading earns its keep when big and short.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-abeezee: ABeeZee reads approachable, its strokes as uniform as neon glass tubing and its terminals clear of the stem, a friendly sans beneath Electroharmonix. Even a long passage would feel unhurried.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-almendra: Gapped letters, commanding presence. Almendra, a classic serif with a deep midsection in the lowercase, follows in dignified, bookish tones, giving Electroharmonix's open-handed curves a more old-fashioned partner.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-cascadia-c: Cascadia Code lays down a wire-like monoline skeleton, its bowls smooth and unobstructed, set against Electroharmonix's gapped display letters. A longer passage would move steadily, with every character plainly separate.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-headland-o: Electroharmonix leads with open gaps between every letter. Headland One, a serif with gentle stroke variation and letters set well apart, would make a long passage feel traditional and dignified.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-roboto: Gaps split each word into single letters in Electroharmonix. Roboto, a plain sans with generous mouths on its round letters, would make a longer passage feel clean and contemporary, never crowded.
